description:
## What

Three RFC-conformance lints deferred from PKIX-9vnx.9.2.1 (which shipped the first 5 of the 8 candidate lints in pkix-lint 0.7.0, 2026-05-12). These three need more substantive implementation work than the straightforward extension-presence / EKU-membership pattern used for the first batch.

## Lints

### 1. `rfc5280::Rfc5280SanRequiredWhenSubjectEmptyLint`

RFC 5280 §4.2.1.6:

> If the subject field contains an empty sequence, then the issuing CA
> MUST include a subjectAltName extension that is marked as critical.

Implementation notes:
- Need to detect "empty subject" — the Subject is a `Name ::= CHOICE { rdnSequence RDNSequence }` where `RDNSequence ::= SEQUENCE OF RelativeDistinguishedName`. Empty means the RDNSequence has zero entries.
- When empty: SAN MUST be present AND marked critical.
- When non-empty: SAN may be absent.

x509-cert `tbs_certificate.subject` is a `Name` type; emptiness check is `cert.tbs_certificate.subject.0.is_empty()`.

Negative-test fixture: would need a cert with empty subject + missing-or-non-critical SAN. Likely needs new fixture generation via pyca/cryptography. Out of scope: actually generating that fixture; the lint impl is shippable now, fixture can come later.

### 2. `rfc5280::Rfc5280SignatureAlgorithmMatchLint`

RFC 5280 §4.1.1.2 + §4.1.2.3:

> This field [`signatureAlgorithm` in Certificate] MUST contain the same
> algorithm identifier as the signature field in the sequence
> tbsCertificate.

Implementation notes:
- Compare `cert.signature_algorithm` (the outer Certificate's algorithm) to `cert.tbs_certificate.signature` (the TBS's algorithm).
- Both are `AlgorithmIdentifier` structs from x509-cert/spki. Need to compare both the OID and the optional parameters (handle the NULL vs absent ambiguity for RSA-with-* signatures: RFC 4055 §2.1 says params SHOULD be NULL for RSA-PKCS1 sigs; some implementations omit them entirely; both are commonly accepted).
- This is a relatively rare bug-class in well-behaved cert issuance but is a real RFC requirement, surfaces malformed certs.

Negative-test fixture: need a cert where the outer and inner algorithm identifiers disagree. Not present in existing fixtures; likely needs custom DER-level synthesis (since pyca/openssl wouldn't normally produce such a cert). Fixture-generation is harder than the lint impl itself.

### 3. `rfc8398::Rfc8398SmimeMailboxEquivalenceLint`

RFC 8398 §3 (last paragraph):

> If both rfc822Name and SmtpUTF8Mailbox are present in the
> subjectAltName extension, then the address values MUST be identical
> with the following exception: any internationalized parts of the
> email address (such as those rendered using A-labels) MUST be encoded
> per the SmtpUTF8Mailbox specification.

Implementation notes:
- Iterate SAN; collect all rfc822Name entries and all id-on-SmtpUTF8Mailbox otherName entries.
- For each pair: check equivalence under the rule above. The "internationalized parts encoded per SmtpUTF8Mailbox" clause means the local-part is UTF-8 in SmtpUTF8Mailbox and A-label-or-ASCII-only in rfc822Name; the domain may differ only by U-label/A-label encoding.
- Requires the `idna` crate (workspace dep) to canonicalize A-labels and U-labels.

Negative-test fixture: need a cert with both rfc822Name AND SmtpUTF8Mailbox SANs that disagree. Likely custom-generated via pyca/cryptography.

## Why deferred

The first 5 lints from PKIX-9vnx.9.2.1 all follow the same pattern: "extension X must be present, extension X must contain element Y". Mechanical. The 3 deferred lints each require additional logic (empty-subject detection, AlgorithmIdentifier equivalence with parameter quirks, IDN-aware UTF-8 equivalence) that adds enough complexity that they want their own commits + fixtures.

PKIX-9vnx.9.2.1 has been kept open (rather than closed) until these three lints land, satisfying its strict "at least one new RFC-conformance Lint impl per candidate above" acceptance criterion.

## Out of scope

- Fixture generation for any negative test. The lint impls can ship with positive tests only against existing fixtures; negative fixtures land when generated. File a follow-on fixture-generation bead if blocking.
- New `IdentityError`-style error wrapping in pkix-chain — these lints feed `LintResult::Error` only.

## Acceptance

- [ ] All 3 lints land as `pub struct` + `impl Lint` in their respective `rfc5280` / `rfc8398` modules.
- [ ] Each carries `spec_section_id` + `spec_url`.
- [ ] At least one passing test per lint (positive case against existing fixtures).
- [ ] Negative cases either tested against new fixtures OR documented as "fixture-gen needed; positive tests only for now".
- [ ] CHANGELOG entry under `pkix-lint`.
- [ ] PKIX-9vnx.9.2.1 closed once this child closes (its 8-candidate acceptance now met).

## Cross-references

- PKIX-9vnx.9.2.1 (parent — 5 of 8 lints shipped)
- PKIX-9vnx.9.2 (grandparent — convenience aliases that consume these lints)
- pkix-lint/src/rfc5280.rs (existing pattern)
- specs/rfc5280.txt §4.2.1.6, §4.1.1.2, §4.1.2.3
- specs/rfc8398.txt §3 (last paragraph)
title: Add 3 deferred RFC-conformance lints (sig-alg match, SAN-when-subject-empty, rfc822/SmtpUTF8 equivalence)
